title: Dal Makhani

ingredients.title: For the Dal
items: Whole black urad dal (sabut urad) – 1 cup (200 g)
Red kidney beans (rajma) – ¼ cup (50 g)

ingredients.title: For the Masala
items: Ghee – 3 tbsp, or 2 tbsp ghee + 1 tbsp butter
Tomatoes – 3 medium, pureed, or 1 cup tomato puree

instruction.title: Soak & Cook the Dal
steps: Wash the urad dal and rajma thoroughly.
Soak both overnight for 8–12 hours.
Drain and rinse the soaked legumes.
Add them to a pressure cooker or heavy-bottomed pot with 4–5 cups water, turmeric, and salt.
Pressure cook for about 8–10 whistles, or simmer in a heavy pot for 1½–2 hours until completely soft.
The lentils should be creamy and mash easily between your fingers.

instruction.title: Prepare the Masala Base
steps: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add chopped onion and sauté until light golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw aroma disappears.
Add tomato puree and cook patiently until it thickens and the ghee begins to separate.
Add Kashmiri red chili powder, coriander powder, garam masala, and slit green chili.
Stir well and cook briefly to bloom the spices.

instruction.title: Combine & Slow Cook
steps: Add the cooked urad dal and rajma mixture along with some of its cooking liquid to the masala.
Mix thoroughly and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook on very low heat for 45–60 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Add small amounts of water if the dal becomes too thick.
Gently mash some of the lentils against the side of the pan to create a naturally creamy texture.

instruction.title: Finish with Cream & Butter
steps: Stir in the fresh cream, butter, and crushed kasuri methi.
Simmer gently for another 10 minutes.
Taste and adjust the salt and consistency.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot.

chefTips: Slow cooking: Traditional dal makhani benefits from several hours of gentle simmering; a heavy pot or slow cooker gives the best creamy texture.
Texture: The dal should become naturally thick and silky from the slow breakdown of the urad and rajma, not from added flour or starch.
Cream: Use enough cream to enrich the dal without overpowering its earthy lentil flavor.
Butter: Adding butter toward the end gives the dish its characteristic rich, glossy finish.
Kasuri methi: Crush the dried fenugreek leaves between your palms before adding to release their aroma.
Smoky finish: For restaurant-style depth, use the dhungar method with a small piece of hot charcoal, a little ghee, and a tightly covered pot for 1–2 minutes.
Resting: Let the finished dal rest for a few minutes before serving; the flavors deepen and the consistency becomes richer.
